analysis: The context before the call: The method `parsePropertyName` takes a `String name` and tokenizes it using a `StringTokenizer` with delimiter '.', adding each token to a `List<String>`. The list `propName` thus contains only `String` objects. The call `propName.toArray(new String[propName.size()])` passes a newly created `String` array of the same size as the list. The `toArray` method documentation declares two exceptions: `ArrayStoreException` (thrown if the runtime type of the specified array is not a supertype of every element in the list) and `NullPointerException` (thrown if the specified array is null). Since the array is of type `String[]` and all elements are `String` objects (which are instances of `String`), the array type is a supertype of all elements, so `ArrayStoreException` is avoided. The array argument is explicitly created with `new String[...]`, which is never null, so `NullPointerException` is also avoided. Therefore, no exceptions from `toArray` can occur in this context.
answer: For each declared exception: ArrayStoreException - its throwing condition is avoided because the list only contains String objects and the array is of type String[], which is a supertype of String. NullPointerException - its throwing condition is avoided because the array argument is not null; it is a newly created String array.
remark: Both `ArrayStoreException` and `NullPointerException` are avoided in this context. `NullPointerException` would require a null array argument, but the code passes `new String[propName.size()]`, which is non-null. `ArrayStoreException` would require an element in the list whose runtime type is not assignable to the array's component type, but the list only contains `String` objects and the array is `String[]`, so no incompatibility exists.
